U06-STRONG-ENDINGS.claim: Present stem supplies imperative and infinitive; bind/bindað, fōh/fōð; infinitives bindan/fōn; tō bindanne/tō fōnne. The -e plural is conditioned by a following subject pronoun.
U06-STRONG-ENDINGS.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-CONTRACTS.claim: Contracted strong singular imperative has final h: long ī in class I, ēo in II, short eo in V, short ea in VI, long ō in VII. Explicit tēoh/seoh/sleah/fōh; wrīh derived from explicitly named wrēon class I.
U06-CONTRACTS.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-WEAK-I.claim: hīer/hīerað, sęle/sęllað, fręme/fręmmað, nęre/nęriað; sęte expressly given. Heavy weak I and short/geminate systems must remain separate; prefixed lexical applications declared.
U06-WEAK-I.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-WEAK-II.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-WEAK-III.claim: hafa/habbað, nafa/nabbað, leofa/libbað (lifiað alternative), saga or sęge/sęcgað, hoga/hycgað. Parenthesized e in sęcg(e)an/hycg(e)an remains an explicit source spelling choice.
U06-WEAK-III.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-PP.claim: Seven selected preterite-present indicative stem systems; witan wite command; Cook mugan and defective citation labels; excluded systems retained in source boundaries.
U06-PP.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-ANOM.claim: Alternate bēo/bist/bið/bēoð; wes/bēo and wesað/bēoð; complete willan/dōn/gān indicative series, explicit dō/dōð and gā/gāð commands; willan has only negative plural imperative in Cook.
U06-ANOM.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-WRIGHT-IMP-INF.claim: Strong imperative singular, ordinary second plural equal to present indicative plural; historical gerund/dative infinitive -enne/-anne; no first/third-person imperative paradigm.
U06-WRIGHT-IMP-INF.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-WRIGHT-WEAK.claim: Short weak imperative preserves -e and simplifies its j-geminate; nere/freme/sete; long dēm, drenc, hyngre, giere and gierwað. īecan/hīeran/lǣdan belong to heavy-stem model.
U06-WRIGHT-WEAK.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-FULK-DEFECTS.claim: Explicitly unattested infinitive citation labels *durran,*sculan,*mōtan,*magan; no formal preterite-present imperative, subjunctive substitutes. Full finite stems remain usable.
U06-FULK-DEFECTS.verification: Original page images visually inspected; OCR is a finding aid only.

U06-FINAL-GEMINATE.claim: Word-final gemination is frequently simplified; heavy weak I distinguishes fyllan/cyssan from settan, whose imperative is expressly sete. Selected cys and prefixed gefyl are declared applications of the heavy-stem ending and simplification, not individually quoted textual attestations. Simplification is not a claim that every final double consonant is forbidden.
U06-FINAL-GEMINATE.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-J-PRESENTS.claim: Explicit bide, hefe, swere; licgan and sittan grouped with biddan; scieppan grouped with hebban. These strong verbs have short weak-I-like present singular imperatives in -e. Course retains Cook hooked e in hefe/swere.
U06-J-PRESENTS.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-J-PRESENTS-CORROBORATION.claim: Explicit site/sittaþ, infinitives sittan/to sittenne; absence of gemination in imperative singular. Lists biddan, licgan, hebban, scieppan, swerian; explains underlying f in hebban and g in licgan. Historical details are evidence, not learner targets.
U06-J-PRESENTS-CORROBORATION.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-INFINITIVE-USE.claim: Uninflected infinitive normal with modal auxiliaries; inflected infinitive after to replaces -an with -enne or -anne, West Saxon usually -anne. Functions partly overlap; purpose is an important use, not an exclusive one. Accusative-and-infinitive, infinitival subjects, and passive interpretations remain outside the selected elementary scope.
U06-INFINITIVE-USE.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-BEON-USE.claim: The beo/bist/bið/beoð series denotes futurity or habitual/gnomic being. The course calls it an alternate present series and supplies an expected-later context for its productive future-state use; it does not claim that every bið is future.
U06-BEON-USE.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-ANOM-CORROBORATION.claim: Complete don/gan/willan indicative paradigms, including explicit dydest/eodest/woldest and preterite plurals; don/gan imperative pairs and inflected infinitives to donne/to ganne. Quantity marks and thorn in the original are retained in the image; course spellings follow Cook.
U06-ANOM-CORROBORATION.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-COMMAND-SYNTAX.claim: Commands with or without second-person subject pronoun. Cook gives beo, wite ðu, and ge eft-hweorfað. Command function is not proof of an inherited regular preterite-present imperative system.
U06-COMMAND-SYNTAX.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-INFINITIVE-SYNTAX.claim: Bare infinitive can follow motion verbs with specification or purpose, while the gerund/inflected infinitive also expresses purpose and other relations. The selected cuman + to-inflected purpose frame must not be described as the only grammatical expression of purpose.
U06-INFINITIVE-SYNTAX.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-WRIGHT-WITAN.claim: Wright explicitly calls wite/witaþ imperative, with plural -aþ borrowed from ordinary present plurals. This functional/traditional classification is reconciled with Fulk no-formal-imperative statement; no witan command pair is assigned here.
U06-WRIGHT-WITAN.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-WRIGHT-MAGAN.claim: Magan is the conventional label corresponding to Cook mugan; meaht later miht, meahte/mehte later mihte are attested source variants. Do not infer an actual infinitive from the unstarred older dictionary label; Fulk explicitly flags the gap.
U06-WRIGHT-MAGAN.verification: Retained original page images visually inspected; OCR used only as a finding aid.

U06-BT-CUNNAN.claim: Cunnan with an infinitive means to know how, to be able through knowledge or skill. Distinct nominal acquaintance/knowledge senses are not assigned.
U06-BT-CUNNAN.verification: Downloaded facsimile directly inspected; searchable entry used only as a finding aid.
U06-BT-CUNNAN.normalization_note: The facsimile is the original witness. Any course example is separately declared new composition; BT acute quantity notation is not silently presented as a macron transcription.

U06-BT-MAGAN.claim: Magan means to be able because an action is possible and occurs with a plain infinitive. The selected elementary use is capacity, including physical ability; epistemic and permission uses are not required.
U06-BT-MAGAN.verification: Downloaded facsimile directly inspected; searchable entry used only as a finding aid.
U06-BT-MAGAN.normalization_note: The facsimile is the original witness. Any course example is separately declared new composition; BT acute quantity notation is not silently presented as a macron transcription.

U06-BT-MOTAN.claim: Permission/being allowed with a plain infinitive, including explicit present licet and past licuit examples. Past moste may mean was allowed to; this assignment does not teach the separate must/be obliged sense.
